focus: the new layout generator port (DungeonLayout.cs), GenStep dressing (plants, remains corpse generation, stuff-made unbreakable wall), and theme selection
diffSource: since build 22 (2026-10-07T20:13:02Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: TUBAD_DungeonWall is both madeFromStuff and saveCompressible: every wall cell errors on load and loses its stone
findings.detail: Compressed saves store only each cell's def hash. MapFileCompressor.ThingsToSpawnAfterLoad rebuilds each compressed thing with ThingMaker.MakeThing(thingDef) and no stuff, and MakeThing logs "is madeFromStuff but stuff=null. Assigning default." for each one, using GenStuff.DefaultStuffFor (BlocksGranite for Stony). The wall has useHitPoints=false, so IsSaveCompressible always passes it. Loading any save with a dungeon map open therefore logs one error per wall cell (thousands) and turns every wall granite-coloured, which undoes this change's purpose. Fix: remove <saveCompressible>true</saveCompressible> (Defs/TUBAD_Dungeon.xml:65) so walls are saved one by one with their stuff.

findings.title: Stuff-made TUBAD_DungeonWall is saveCompressible: every wall reloads without its stuff and logs an error
findings.detail: GenStep_DungeonLayout now spawns every wall as MakeThing(TUBAD_DungeonWall, blocks), and the def has madeFromStuff=true while still saveCompressible=true. A compressed thing is stored as its def's short hash only and rebuilt on load with ThingMaker.MakeThing(thingDef) with no stuff (MapFileCompressor.cs:102). That logs 'is madeFromStuff but stuff=null. Assigning default.' once per wall cell, thousands on a large dungeon, on every load of a save with a dungeon map, and the walls lose their rock colour. The walls are always compressible: useHitPoints=false, spawned, never referenced. One change fixes it: remove <saveCompressible>true</saveCompressible> from TUBAD_DungeonWall (Defs/TUBAD_Dungeon.xml:65) so each wall is saved in full with its stuff.

findings.title: A failed Carve on a spanning-tree link strands every chamber behind it
findings.detail: Build carves each chosen link once and keeps only the successes. When TryDoor finds no straight wall facing free rock, or AStar returns null, the minimum spanning tree just loses that link: nothing retries the next-shortest pair that would rejoin the two groups. Compile then fills back in everything the exit cannot reach, so one failed door on a built room can drop its whole subtree, not just itself. One fix at this line: when a tree link fails, walk the sorted pairs for the next one joining the same two groups and carve that.

findings.title: The squeeze's locked ring can cut the link's own tunnel
findings.detail: The radius-2.6 ring of locked rock is stamped before the rest of the path is carved, and the carve loop skips locked cells (line 502). The pinch check only tests path cells p-2..p+2 and the distance of p-3/p+3. If the path bends back into the ring anywhere else, that cell stays rock and the link is broken; Compile then fills in whatever only that link reached. Reject a pinch spot if any path cell outside pinch±2 falls inside the ring.

findings.title: BlocksOf takes the chunk's first butcher product without checking it is a stuff
findings.detail: BlocksOf returns rock.building.mineableThing.butcherProducts.FirstOrDefault().thingDef and only falls back to BlocksGranite on null. If a modded rock's chunk butchers into something that is not a stuff, ThingMaker.MakeThing logs 'Tried to make ... which is not a stuff' for every wall cell and door at line 128/133 (ThingMaker.cs:10-13). Add `?.IsStuff == true` (or stuffProps.CanMake(TUBAD_DungeonWall)) to the return so the BlocksGranite fallback applies.

findings.title: Plugs no longer gate every link between caverns
findings.detail: Links out of chamber 0 never squeeze, pinchChance is below 1, loop links are added between near neighbours, and cavern blobs can overlap (blob reach is about 1.3r), so a plug can often be walked around. The new summary only promises this for built-room doors, so it looks intended. Phase 4, which places creatures by chamber, should not assume a plug seals what lies beyond it.

findings.title: A* distance estimate overshoots
findings.detail: A step through open space costs 0.5 but the estimate is Manhattan distance at 1 per cell, so paths are not guaranteed cheapest and cells get re-expanded. Harmless at 60-150 cell maps and arguably adds the intended wander.

findings.title: The saved DungeonSite.theme does not do what its comment says
findings.detail: Each entry makes a new DungeonSite (DungeonEntry.cs:88), so site.theme is always null when the map is generated and ThemeFor picks the theme every time. 'Same tile, same theme' comes from ThemeFor's seed (world seed plus tile); the saved field only keeps the theme fixed for one visit. Worth rewording the comment so nobody relies on the field for consistency across parties.

findings.title: Frozen and Flooded both use priority 3, so cold swampy tiles get a 50/50 theme pick
findings.detail: ThemeFor keeps only the top-priority matching themes and breaks ties by commonality (both 1). A tile at or below -4 average temperature with swampiness of at least 0.4 gets either theme, fixed per tile. If one should win, give it priority 4.

findings.title: Theme seed ignores the PlanetTile layer
findings.detail: ThemeFor seeds from the world seed and tile.tileId only. A dungeon with the same tileId on another world layer gets the same theme roll. This is cosmetic. Adding the tile's layer to the hash would separate them.

findings.title: Root tangle and sand drift inherit stone rubble filth from BuildingNaturalBase
findings.detail: BuildingNaturalBase sets filthLeaving Filth_RubbleRock, and TUBAD_PlugBase does not override it, so hacking out roots or digging out sand leaves rock rubble. Override filthLeaving per plug if that matters.

findings.title: Rare themes without <biomes> skip their numeric ranges
findings.detail: The rare roll checks `t.biomes.NullOrEmpty() || t.Matches(info)`, so a rare theme with no biome list is chosen anywhere, whatever temperature/rainfall/swampiness/plantDensity it declares. The only rare theme today, TUBAD_Crypt, sets no ranges, so nothing goes wrong yet. Using just `t.Matches(info)` would follow the documented matching rules for future or modded rare themes.
